on april 12, 2026, a routine high‑pressure inspection of the 38‑inch natgas transmission line between milepost 102.3 and 105.8 in the valley of the northern sierras revealed a localized deformation in a 2‑inch flange section of the secondary 20‑inch riser. the line was operating at 680 psig when a moderate seismic event (magnitude 4.2) struck the region at 03:14 utc. seismic sensors recorded a 0.35‑meter ground displacement directly over the pipeline corridor, with ground acceleration exceeding 0.12 g at the riser. during the post‑event pressure test, the riser exhibited a sudden pressure drop from 680 to 320 psig, and a leak was detected at the flange face. field crews shut down the segment, isolated it with valve 3‑1‑2, and evacuated the line to 30 psig. visual inspection showed a 0.8‑inch crack in the weld of the flange, accompanied by a 1.2‑inch dent in the pipe wall. a 4‑inch burst pipe was then replaced, welded with a 90‑degree fillet, and the new section was pressure tested to 750 psig for 48 hours before returning to service. the incident was classified as natural‑force damage caused by seismic activity.

on february 12, 2025, at 10:45 a.m. (est) the mountain view transmission company (mvtc) monitoring center received a call from the county emergency management office in grand valley, colorado, reporting a sudden rupture on the mvtc 24‑inch natural gas pipeline near the confluence of the river. the affected segment, located between meter markers 12,300 and 12,450, was operating at 920 psig and transporting propylene at a flow rate of 6,500 mcf/d. at 11:10 a.m., the control room operator observed a rapid drop in pressure from 915 psig to 520 psig, triggering a scada alarm. the incident crew arrived on site at 11:45 a.m. after a 25‑minute response interval. upon arrival, they observed extensive ground deformation and a 2‑meter high displacement of the surrounding earth, consistent with a micro‑seismic event that had occurred at 10:30 a.m. the pipeline had been displaced by an estimated 1.8 meters, causing a longitudinal fracture across the weld seam of the 6‑in. pipe. the ruptured section was isolated and capped with a temporary pressure relief valve. emergency crews performed a visual inspection and the damaged segment was marked for removal. the pipeline was temporarily shut down until a full failure analysis could be completed. the 48‑hour update to the national response center was submitted on february 13, 2025, with report no. 1456329. the laboratory analysis confirmed that the rupture was due to a sudden ground movement that exceeded the pipe’s bending fatigue limits, leading to a brittle fracture. a replacement segment will be installed using a 24‑in. seamless steel pipe with a 1,050 psig maximum operating pressure, and the line will be re‑commissioned in spring 2025.

on 05/08/2024 at 04:32 pm cdt a magnitude 5.7 earthquake struck the western foothills, producing severe ground motion. the seismic event caused a 20‑inch schedule 80 stainless steel line to shift 12 inches horizontally, resulting in a 4‑inch longitudinal crack at the 48‑in. weld near wellhead 42. at the time of the shift, the line was operating at 2,000 psi and 12,500 scf/min. the crack allowed an estimated 1,200 scf/min of natural gas to escape, generating a plume that drifted up the canyon. field crews were alerted by the gas monitoring system at 04:38 pm. the main line was isolated by the gate valve at 04:45 pm and vented through a portable flaring unit. a temporary 4‑inch patch weld was applied to the cracked section for

on march 14, 2025, a sudden flash flood in the upper valley of the blue river caused the removal of soil around the support posts of the 24‑inch corrugated steel gas pipeline owned by energy supply co. the pipeline, running parallel to the floodplain for 2.5 km, was operating at 580 psig. as the water level rose to 6 meters above the normal riverbed, the supports under the 12‑inch transition joint at mile marker 12.4 lost footing. within 15 minutes the pipe settled 30 cm laterally, creating a 45‑degree bend at the weld between the 24‑inch line and the 12‑inch fitting. when the bend exceeded the allowable stress limit of 400 psi, a sudden fracture occurred at the weld root, releasing natural gas into the atmosphere. field crew responded at 12:37 p.m., shut down the line by closing the upstream 12‑inch isolation valve (c12‑217). pressure dropped from 580 to 120 psig. a gas leak detector confirmed a 5‑meter plume at 2:10 p.m. the rupture was inspected, the damaged segment was capped with a 24‑inch fusion weld, and a new support assembly was installed. the company performed a root‑cause analysis and will upgrade the support system with geotextile reinforcement.

at 3:12 pm on august 17 2022, a severe wind event associated with the passage of tropical storm alex struck the red river natural gas line near mile 12 of the north branch. the 24‑inch high‑strength carbon steel line, operating at 3 500 psi, suffered a 2‑inch radial breach after a large fallen oak branch impacted the pipe and caused a localized stress concentration. the rupture released approximately 18.9 million cubic feet of natural gas into the surrounding farmland. a nearby safety relief valve tripped within 2 seconds of the rupture, venting gas to the atmosphere at 1 200 psi. an enbridge field crew was dispatched at 3:45 pm, isolated the rupture by shutting the nearest isolation valves at 4:10 pm, and conducted a pressure test of the remaining line at 3 500 psi to ensure integrity. the incident was reported to the state environmental agency within 90 minutes and was logged under incident 22‑08‑004. a subsequent investigation indicated that the failure was caused by a combination of wind‑induced branch impact and a pre‑existing corrosion defect at the weld joint. training updates will include enhanced inspection protocols for branches near high‑pressure lines.

post winter storm winter storm zephyr slammed a 40" steel transmission line owned by midwest energy on the rangelands of nebraska. the line, operating at 3500 psi, suffered a catastrophic rupture at a 3/8" weld seam near a maintenance hatch, likely due to ice accretion and subsequent thermal contraction. upon automated pressure drop detection, the remote control system closed the upstream isolation valve and the downstream relief valve opened to 250 psi to protect downstream facilities. field crews isolated the section and a rapid leak assessment confirmed a 12‑foot breach. the damaged segment was tagged for abandonment, and the pipeline operator initiated a containment plan that included temporary steel containment sleeves and a controlled depressurization to 100 psi. the remaining intact line was inspected by roving crew, and a replacement splice was scheduled for the following week. the incident was reported to the regulatory body, and the operator is currently evaluating the structural integrity of adjacent segments for potential freeze‑damage.

on may 12 2024 at approximately 3:15 am local time a severe thunderstorm with wind speeds exceeding 60 mph and a localized storm surge of 3.2 feet struck the 26‑inch diameter, schedule 80, 316 stainless steel natural gas main that traverses the east bank of the river in the township of springfield. a 1‑inch diameter branch from a mature oak tree fell onto the pipe near mile marker 42.7, causing a sudden drop in internal pressure from 580 psig to 0 psig and a rapid rupture of a 2‑inch circumferential weld. the rupture released an estimated 1,200,000 cubic feet of gas into the atmosphere over a 3‑minute interval, producing an audible explosion and a fireball that ignited the surrounding vegetation. fire suppression teams were dispatched within 4 minutes of the first call at 3:19 am and established a perimeter by 3:27 am. the mainline isolation valve at mp 43.1 was closed by the control room crew at 3:35 am, halting further gas flow. a preliminary investigation by the state pipeline safety office indicated that the failure was due to the impact of the falling limb, with no evidence of corrosion or material defect. the incident was reported to the nrc at 3:45 am after the rupture was confirmed. by 5:15 am the fire was fully extinguished and the affected zone was cleared of debris. 

6/1/2024 update: the damaged pipe segment has been replaced with a new 26‑inch schedule 80 carbon steel line and a 3‑inch high‑pressure relief valve was installed to mitigate future natural force events. no property damage or injuries were recorded, and the surrounding wildlife habitat has been restored.

on april 18, 2024, at 04:32 a.m. eastern time, the north coast of texas experienced an unexpected surge of high seas from a passing tropical storm that pushed water levels to 12.5 feet above normal. at that time a 16‑inch, 60‑year‑old, high‑strength carbon‑steel pipeline, rated at 200 psi, was transporting 1.2 million barrels of crude oil from the offshore platform “seabreeze” to the onshore storage facility “shorepoint.” the surge exerted lateral pressures on the buried section of the pipe, located 300 feet below the ocean surface, and the pipe’s cathodic protection system was temporarily disabled by the corrosive seawater intrusion. at 06:45 a.m. the pipeline monitoring system detected a sudden drop in pressure to 42 psi and a concurrent rise in flow‑line temperature, indicating a partial rupture. a crew of 12 was dispatched from the coastal operations center; by 07:15 a.m. divers confirmed a 2‑inch breach near the third bend of the pipe, where a 3‑foot‑deep trench had recently been excavated for maintenance. the breach was temporarily capped with a pressure‑resistant clamp that withstood 180 psi before the clamp was fully secured. the incident was reported to the national response center within 30 minutes of detection, and the offshore platform’s emergency shut‑off was activated at 08:10 a.m., preventing further release. the clamp was replaced with a permanent repair segment during the following night shift, and full‑pressure operations resumed by 10:45 a.m. on the same day.

on the afternoon of march 15, 2024, a 2.5‑meter, 120‑psi, 20‑inch carbon steel transmission line that traverses the eastern foothills of the colorado basin experienced a sudden rupture after a series of seismic tremors. the line, operating at 115 psi during the event, was interrupted at a welded flange located 18.3 km downstream of the mid‑western compressor station. field crews observed a 3‑meter fissure in the pipe wall and a sharp drop in the line pressure to 20 psi within minutes. a burst of flammable gas was released into the surrounding valley, prompting an immediate alarm and the activation of the station’s emergency shutdown protocol.

the operations team isolated the affected segment by closing the nearest isolation valves and sealed the ruptured section with a temporary c‑shaped repair collar rated for 150 psi. safety personnel secured a 500‑meter perimeter, and the incident command system was activated. environmental, health & safety staff conducted a vapor plume survey, confirming that the leak was contained within the designated containment zone. a geotechnical assessment was initiated to investigate potential ground motion effects on the pipeline alignment.

a field inspection team confirmed a 1.5‑inch reduction in wall thickness at the weld. a full‑scale repair was scheduled for the following week, with the segment slated to be replaced with a 22‑inch, 10% carbon steel pipe rated to 200 psi. the line was restored to service on april 4, 2024, after a pressure test of 135 psi confirmed integrity.

on 3/12/23 at 08:45 am, a magnitude‑6.2 earthquake struck the foothills of the mesa region, causing a sudden lateral displacement of the earth over the 36‑inch schedule‑80 carbon steel hq‑24 pipeline. the pipeline, operating at 6,500 psi in a 16‑inch stainless steel branch, had a weld‑to‑pipe joint (t‑joint) at the 2,400‑foot marker that was previously inspected in 2021 (irn 12.3). the seismic event produced an 8‑foot uplift of the soil, bending the pipe about 0.5 inches at the joint and creating a 0.75‑inch longitudinal crack that propagated along the weld toe. a pressure transducer on the downstream side registered a drop from 6,500 psi to 3,200 psi within 12 seconds. field crews responded via the 911 emergency line and reported the pressure loss to the control center at 08:58 am. the rupture was located by an automatic shut‑off valve at 09:05 am, followed by a visual inspection of the cracked segment at 09:20 am. the cracked weld was removed and replaced with a new 16‑inch forged carbon steel pipe section, heat‑treated and coated with 7200‑type epoxy. the incident was reported to the national response center by 10:10 am. a root‑cause analysis concluded that the natural seismic activity exceeded the design lateral load capacity, leading to joint separation and failure. the pipeline was re‑commissioned at 02:45 pm after pressure testing at 6,200 psi confirmed integrity.

at approximately 2:10 pm cdt on august 18, 2018, southwestern gas transmission, a subsidiary of western utilities, received a phone call from the north bank of the colorado river about a sudden loss of pressure on line 23‑b, a 24‑inch api 5l steel transmission line operating at 800 psig. the crew dispatched to the field found the line had developed a significant crack near a girth weld at the downstream end of the river crossing. inspection photographs revealed the supporting concrete foundation had been eroded by a recent flood event that had exceeded the 100‑year flood level, exposing the pipeline to scour. the loss of support allowed a free‑span segment to sag and experience vortex‑induced vibration at the flood’s peak flow rate of 4,200 cfs. the oscillations produced a fatigue crack that propagated to a 0.5‑inch transverse fissure, ultimately causing the line to rupture and release gas into the river corridor. the rupture was detected when a remote pressure monitoring system reported a rapid drop to atmospheric pressure. the incident was reported to the state public service commission, phmsa, and the national response center within 15 minutes. subsequent root‑cause analysis attributed the failure to accelerated erosion of the concrete abutment and the lack of a protective berm, both exacerbated by the high water velocity during the flood event.

on april 18, 2025, a severe thunderstorm with sustained wind speeds exceeding 70 mph moved across the north‑central region, producing intense rainfall and flash flooding along the south‑ridge corridor. at 1012 hrs, operators of the 30‑inch, schedule 80 carbon‑steel line (p# 4501) located near the creek bend experienced a sudden drop in downstream pressure from 210 psig to 0 psig, indicating a rupture. field crews noted a 5‑inch diameter gouge in the pipe wall adjacent to a shallow embankment that had recently been eroded by the floodwaters. the rupture was located at a weld joint that had been installed in 2017 and had never been inspected for corrosion after the 2019 flood event. immediately after the loss, the relief valve on the upstream flare line opened, venting 2.5 mmcf of natural gas to the atmosphere. emergency response teams were dispatched within 12 minutes, and the leak was capped using a temporary repair collar and a 1‑inch epoxy patch. a full hydraulic and seismic survey was conducted, revealing that the soil displacement had shifted the pipe alignment, causing the weld to fail under the combined thermal and mechanical loads. corrective action included relocating the pipe segment to a more stable subgrade, installing a support beam, and conducting a 2‑year inspection cycle. the incident investigation determined that the primary cause was the combined effects of intense rainfall, rapid groundwater rise, and soil erosion, which together compromised the structural integrity of the pipeline.

on a sunny monday afternoon, a municipal construction crew was excavating a new sidewalk near the intersection of 4th and market streets. a hydraulic backhoe operator inadvertently struck a 30‑inch carbon‑steel natural gas main operating at 220 psig. the impact caused a transverse break in the pipe and released a burst of gas that drifted into an adjacent open trench. at 9:15 a.m., the crew realized the leak, stopped excavation, and called the local gas company. by 9:45 a.m., the company's emergency response team arrived and located the rupture at the junction of pipe #12 and valve #27. they isolated the line by closing isolation valve #27 and shut off the adjacent pressure relief valve. the burst pipe was cut at the break and a 12‑inch repair section was welded in place, followed by a 4‑hour purging cycle to remove residual gas. the repaired line was re‑pressurized to 180 psig at 11:00 a.m. pressure testing verified integrity. the crew was retrained on excavation procedures and a new signage system was installed to prevent future incidents. no injuries or property damage were reported.

on 12/03/2023 at 08:27, a heavy‑duty excavator operated by a local contractor struck a 10‑inch diameter carbon steel line located at 3,200 psi operating pressure on the east side of the facility. the impact caused a 2.5‑inch segment to shear. the rupture released approximately 5,000 barrels of crude oil into the surrounding soil. gas control was notified at 08:35, and the emergency response team initiated a containment strategy. the line was shut by a field valve at 08:40, and pressure dropped from 3,200 psi to 1,000 psi within 12 minutes. subsequent inspection revealed a localized circumferential crack on the pipe surface at the impact site. a post‑incident investigation determined that the excavator was operating within 12 feet of the pipeline, violating the 25‑foot separation requirement. the contractor was notified of the violation, and a corrective action plan was issued. the incident report was filed with the phmsa under § 5.13. no injuries were reported, and the environmental release was contained within the designated buffer zone. the pipe was replaced and the section was retrofitted with a protective coating.

05/12/2024 02:15- stormwatch center received a 3.0 magnitude swell warning for the southeast coast of texas. at 03:10, a local fishing vessel, the "sea fisher", lost steering control due to heavy seas and collided with a buried 12 inch stainless steel line in the gulf of mexico. at 03:30, field crew from the control center received a report of a rupture on the pipeline. the pipeline was operating at 4,500 psig and 12 inches diameter, corroded but in service for 8 years. at 03:45, field crew dispatched 2 emergency units to the incident location. at 04:10, first response team arrived on site and observed a 3 foot gap in the pipe and a 1.5 meter long section of pipe displaced. at 04:20, the team established a safety perimeter and set up a temporary shutdown valve at 06:00. at 05:00, the control center executed a pressure relief procedure and the line was brought to 1,000 psig. at 06:30, a repair crew from the pipeline operator arrived and began cutting the damaged pipe section and welding a 12 inch replacement. at 09:45, pressure was restored to 4,200 psig and flow resumed. at 10:30, the incident was closed and the pipeline was monitored for 48 hours for leaks.

on july 12, 2024, a heavy rainfall event produced a 12‑inch storm surge that saturated the soil surrounding a 30‑ft high embankment supporting a 20‑inch schedule 80 steel gas transmission line (line 405) operating at 550 psi. the saturated soil lost cohesion, causing a localized slope failure that moved a 6‑foot segment of the pipeline horizontally into a shallow trench. the movement breached the pipe, creating a 3‑inch radial tear that produced a rapid pressure drop from 550 psi to 200 psi and released an estimated 8000 gallons of natural gas into the surrounding wetland. at 0215 local dispatch received a distress signal from a nearby electric substation operator, who reported a sudden gas odor and a localized fire. emergency response units were dispatched from the county fire department and the state oil and gas emergency management office. at 0230 the line was isolated using the remote valve system, and the pressure was reduced to 150 psi to prevent further rupture. by 0300 the breach was contained, and a field crew began an inspection that confirmed a 3‑inch longitudinal crack. a repair crew was mobilized at 0800 and completed a full‑length pipe replacement (20‑inch schedule 80 steel) by 1800. the incident was reported to the national response center and no injuries or customer interruptions occurred.

on july 10, 2024 at approximately 1035 hrs. the west branch of the national gas transmission system, a 30‑inch x 2‑inch stainless steel line, was impacted by an excavator operating on the adjacent county road. the bulldozer's hydraulic arm collided with the line's support footing, causing a 4‑inch vertical displacement of the pipe and a 1‑inch break in the outer pipe wall. the high‑pressure flow (950 psi) resulted in a sudden release of natural gas, which ignited in the surrounding vegetation. emergency crews from the regional operations center were dispatched at 1045 hrs. the line was isolated at the nearest shut‑off valve, located 0.3 miles downstream, and a temporary emergency shut‑off was installed using a 12‑inch double‑walled steel fitting. gas control operators confirmed zero pressure at the downstream end by 1105 hrs. a mobile firefighting unit extinguished the flare zone by 1115 hrs. the damaged segment was removed and replaced with a 30‑inch x 2‑inch seamless steel section fabricated by smith & co. the new section was welded in‑place, pressure‑tested to 1200 psi, and the line was re‑energized at 1415 hrs. post‑incident inspection revealed no other damage, and service was restored to the affected communities by 1500 hrs. a full investigation confirmed that the damage was caused by the excavator's hydraulic arm exceeding the pipe’s support clearance.

on 7/12/2024 at 08:45 a 75‑ton tractor towing a 2,000‑lb trailer collided with a 30‑inch schedule 40 api 1063 steel line near a 6‑inch ball valve at milepost 42.3. the impact severed the line and displaced the valve body, causing a 5‑ft fragment of the valve seal to puncture the adjacent pipe. the crew immediately shut the line in and isolated the segment, depressurizing from 900 psi to 200 psi under the control of the operations center. pressure was monitored through a remote transmitter; the reading dropped to 0 psi within 3 min of isolation. a field inspection crew arrived within 12 min and confirmed a 10‑in. crack on the valve stem and a 4‑in. gouge on the pipe wall. the pipeline was shut for 90 min, after which a 120‑ft segment was removed with a hydraulic excavator and replaced with a 30‑inch api 1063 pipe section bolted to the existing line. the new section was inspected by an accredited inspector who verified proper torque and seal integrity. the valve was rebuilt, and the line was slowly re‑pressurised to 850 psi over 45 min while monitoring for leaks. a post‑repair survey confirmed no residual damage and the line was returned to service. the site was secured with temporary barricades until the area was cleared for traffic.

on 7/15/2023, midwest pipelines, inc. (mpi) received a notification from the county sheriff’s office that a construction grader had collided with an underground 12‑inch schedule 80 steel transmission line during a road expansion project. the collision punctured the pipe at the 2,500‑ft location, causing a minor leak that was detected by the pipeline’s pressure monitoring system at 1,250 psi. field crews arrived within 45 minutes, isolated the section by shutting the nearest pressure relief valve and the downstream control valve. they performed a pressure test at 1,300 psi to confirm the integrity of adjacent pipe. the damaged 12‑inch section was removed and replaced with a new 12‑inch schedule 80 steel pipe of 10‑ft length, welded using a butt weld with a 3% phosphorus content to ensure corrosion resistance. the incident was logged as outside‑force damage, and a detailed investigation was conducted to confirm that the construction equipment was operating outside the designated safety zone. the incident report noted that the county’s construction permits had a clause requiring the placement of a temporary protective barrier at all high‑pressure line crossings, which was missing in this case. no injuries were reported, and the line was brought back into service after 14 hours of downtime.

on june 12, 2024 at approximately 0830 hours, a local agricultural tractor equipped with a 4‑ton mower blade collided with the 6‑inch carbon steel transmission line 134b, located along the eastern bank of the riverbend farm. the impact fractured the pipe, causing a rapid release of natural gas at 250 psi. the gas plume was detected by the nearby automatic leak detection system within 5 minutes, triggering an automatic shutdown of the upstream compressor station at 0900. a field crew arrived within 10 minutes and isolated the line at the nearest shut‑off valve, which was located 2.3 km downstream. the fracture was contained within a 20‑foot section of pipe. repairs were completed by 1400, with the line tested to 300 psi before re‑commissioning. no personnel were injured and no ignition occurred. the incident was reported to the state energy regulator and the local fire department, and the total estimated cost of repairs was approximately $65,000. highway 42 was temporarily closed for safety inspections.

on 7/9/2024, during routine shut‑in of the 10‑inch 316l carbon steel mainline in the north‑shelf waterway, a vessel anchored near the 15‑mile stretch of the 12‑inch feeder line lost its moorings during a sudden squall. the drifting anchor chain struck the 12‑inch line, causing a 3‑inch radial breach and instant loss of 1100 psi operating pressure. the 10‑inch line, with a 3‑inch threaded connector, was severed near the 28‑kft depth. the incident was detected when the automated shutdown system reported zero pressure on the 10‑inch line at 0420 hrs. a subsequent sonar survey confirmed a 12‑inch pipe segment had been displaced by 18 feet. the anchor impact also cracked a 6‑inch buried side‑arm, which was isolated at 0445 hrs. a 48‑hour repair window was scheduled; the damaged pipe was replaced with a 12‑inch 304l tube, and the anchor chain was removed after a 3‑day search.

in the early afternoon of march 14, 2025, a municipal garbage truck operating on the westbound lane of interstate 95 veered off the shoulder due to an unexpected loss of traction on a wet patch. the vehicle struck an exposed 24‑inch diameter, 316 stainless steel cross‑arm that supported a 22‑inch diameter, 350‑psi natural gas line running beneath the highway. the impact sheared the cross‑arm, severing the gas line and causing an instantaneous loss of pressure that dropped from 350 psi to zero within seconds. the pipe fractured cleanly at the flange joint, releasing a plume of gas that was quickly detected by the gas monitoring system in the nearby compressor station located 2.3 miles north. emergency response teams from the state emergency services were dispatched within 4 minutes and arrived on site at 1:23 pm. the compressor station operators isolated the affected line and performed a controlled vent to depressurize the 22‑inch pipe segment, preventing any ignition. no injuries were reported and no evacuation was required due to the quick isolation. the damaged 22‑inch line was temporarily capped with a welded steel splice and a repair was completed at 9:45 pm, restoring the 350‑psi service pressure to the downstream distribution network. the incident was reported to the phmsa within 24 hours and a full investigation determined the cause as vehicle collision with the exposed pipeline.

at approximately 2:45 pm on may 12, 2024, a storm surge caused a large fallen tree to collide with a 24‑inch corrugated steel natural gas transmission line owned by northern pipeline company, located 450 feet east of the county's central gas station. the line was operating at 750 psi and had been scheduled for maintenance the previous week. the tree's impact fractured the pipe at a 90‑degree elbow located below grade, resulting in a rapid pressure drop to 200 psi and a sudden release of natural gas. an operator on the local monitoring system received a pressure alarm at 2:48 pm and immediately notified the control center. the control room crew closed the downstream isolation valve, valve id 1325, and the upstream control valve id 1340, causing the affected segment to blow down. within 5 minutes the gas escaped into an adjacent field, where a small fire ignited. the crew contained the blaze by 2:57 pm and the gas was extinguished by 3:12 pm. a subsequent inspection revealed that the pipe had been fractured at a weld joint, likely due to the tree's impact. the damaged section, 30 feet in length, was replaced with a 24‑inch seamless steel pipe. no personnel injuries were reported.

on january 10, 2024, the central monitoring center received a call from the on‑site crew of a local forestry company regarding a sudden loss of pressure on transmission line d-317 located in the east valley of colorado. the line, a 24‑inch schedule 80 steel pipe operating at 2,400 psi, was carrying 450,000 bcf of natural gas when the event was reported. inspection photos taken at the site showed a 3‑inch diameter breach in the pipe where a heavy‑duty logging truck had struck the line during a routine road maintenance operation. the truck’s hydraulic front axle, approximately 1,200 kg, had been traveling along the right‑of‑way without the proper flagging in place. the breach caused an instantaneous loss of 120,000 bcf of gas to the atmosphere, with a total vented volume of 110,000 bcf. the loss was calculated to exceed $70,000, triggering a mandatory report to the federal energy regulatory body. emergency crews closed the line, isolated the affected segment, and performed a controlled blowdown. after a 4‑hour pressure test, a 12‑foot replacement section was welded in place, and service to the downstream distribution network was restored by 12:45 pm.

on july 12, 2024 at 08:43 am local time, midland natural gas received a call from the county road services office reporting a sudden drop in pressure on the 8‑inch stainless steel line that runs parallel to county road 17 south of townville, ar. the crew was dispatched within fifteen minutes and arrived at 09:02 am. they found a 1.5‑inch steel valve riser that had been punctured by a large oak branch that had fallen onto the pipeline during a recent thunderstorm. the branch had breached the pipe wall, causing a rapid release of gas at about 3500 psi. a field crew closed the upstream block valve located 12 feet downstream and evacuated the area to a 500‑foot safety radius. a repair team replaced the damaged riser section with a 1.5‑inch forged steel segment and installed a new 1.5‑inch blind flange. the line was brought back to service at 15:20 after a pressure test at 3500 psi confirmed a leak rate of less than 1 lb/hr. the estimated repair cost exceeded $68,200. a post‑incident inspection of the surrounding area identified no additional risks, and the incident was logged under the external force damage report.

on saturday, june 14th 2023, at approximately 0830 hrs, a residential fire crew using a hydraulic jack to support a collapsed utility pole inadvertently contacted a 30‑inch diameter, 420‑psi polyethylene (pe‑80) gas transmission line buried 6 feet below the surface in north carolina. the jack’s hydraulic cylinder extended beyond its intended scope, causing the tip to break through the soil and strike the pipe. the impact produced a 3‑inch longitudinal fracture at the weld seam, leading to a rapid release of natural gas at an estimated 450 psi. the gas plume ignited by a nearby unattended spark from the crew’s generator, resulting in a 15‑meter radius burn. the crew reported that the incident occurred after the jack was set on a sloped embankment and the ground shifted, causing the jack arm to slide onto the pipeline. the incident was reported to the local fire department, which evacuated the surrounding area. the pipeline company performed a 2‑week shutdown for repairs, installing a new 30‑inch schedule 80 steel replacement segment and applying a 2‑inch diameter steel sleeve to reinforce the weld joint. post‑repair inspections verified integrity before resuming service.

on april 12 2024, a 24‑in carbon steel transmission line, rated 2000 psi and 0.75‑inch wall thickness, located 12 km offshore near the tampa bay shoreline, suffered a rupture when a commercial bottom‑fishing trawler’s net became entangled with the pipe at a 30‑ft deep bend. as the crew hauled the net out of the water, a segment of the net snapped against the pipe, severing the line and creating a 20‑foot long breach. pressure dropped instantly from 2000 psi to 0 psi, and a 200‑barrel oil spill was released into the water column. an emergency response team isolated the damaged segment within 45 minutes, shut the line, and commenced containment and repair operations. the incident caused no injuries but resulted in a small environmental impact. the pipe was made of 20‑cf steel and had been operating at a steady flow of 15,000 barrels per day before the failure. the damage was attributed to an external mechanical force unrelated to any operational activity.

on the afternoon of february 5, 2026, a 30‑inch high‑pressure natural gas transmission line (copper‑coated steel) crossing the riviere valley was struck by a collapsed irrigation ditch during a sudden flash flood. the floodwater carried a large volume of debris, including a broken concrete retaining wall segment that impacted the pipeline near the 45‑mile marker. the impact fractured a 2‑inch weld joint and severed a 10‑inch segment of the main line. the line pressure was operating at 850 psi at the time of the incident, resulting in an estimated 12,000 scf of natural gas released to the atmosphere before the automated shutdown system closed the upstream valve. the gas was subsequently vented through the line pack. emergency crews isolated the damaged section by closing the downstream safety valve and installing an emergency plug at the upstream section. the damaged 10‑inch pipe was removed, a new 10‑inch section was welded in place, and a pressure test of 1,100 psi was performed before reinstating service. the incident was reported to the state regulator and the final repair cost totaled $68,000, exceeding the reporting threshold.

at approximately 16:45 hrs on october 3, 2025, a severe derecho event produced wind gusts exceeding 90 mph. a large oak tree located within 150 ft of the 8‑inch, 2400 psi, carbon steel main collapsed, striking the pipe near segment 15.3 km of the line. the impact caused a 5‑inch diameter rupture and immediate loss of pressure to the downstream service valves. emergency response crews from the state fire marshal, local county sheriff, and the pipeline company mobilized within 30 minutes. the main was isolated at the nearest upstream valve located 2.5 miles upstream. the collapsed tree was removed using a backhoe and hydraulic lift. pressure testing was performed at 1200 psi to confirm integrity before recommissioning. the line was temporarily shut down for 5 hours; service to 12 residential customers was restored by 08:00 hrs on october 4. incident report filed with the state environmental protection agency. no injuries reported, but a nearby residential property sustained roof damage from the falling branches. all relevant regulatory bodies were notified per the incident reporting protocol.

on june 12, 2024, the west texas pipelines, llc reported a rupture of the 30‑inch, schedule 80, 1400 psi natural gas pipeline located in the eastern panhandle. a construction crew from a nearby oilfield facility was excavating a trench 2 m from the pipeline and inadvertently struck the pipe with a jack‑hammer, causing a circumferential crack. approximately 82,500 mcf of natural gas was released, leading to an explosion that ignited a flash‑fire 15 m from the rupture site. the incident resulted in a minor burn to the pipeline’s support structure and a fire that burned for 4 minutes before being extinguished by the local fire department. the pipeline was shut down, the damaged section was inspected, and the gas was isolated. the investigation concluded that the damage was caused by outside force, specifically construction equipment impact, and the incident was deemed reportable under the national incident reporting system. no injuries were reported.

on july 9, 2024 at approximately 10:45am, a 50‑foot tower crane operated by a local construction firm collided with a 30‑inch carbon‑steel natural gas pipeline located beneath the new overpass on east 5th street. the pipeline, operated by northstate utilities, was carrying gas at a design pressure of 1200 psi. the crane’s swing arm struck the pipe near a 4‑inch flared joint, causing a visible fracture and a subsequent 1‑inch gas leak. the crew immediately shut off the main control valve and activated the emergency shut‑off at the nearest regulator station. emergency responders from the county fire department arrived within 5 minutes and contained the leak with a temporary epoxy seal. the incident was reported to the state agency the following day. a detailed inspection by the pipeline operator revealed a 2‑inch longitudinal crack in the pipe wall at the fracture site. the damaged section was removed and replaced with a new 30‑inch schedule 40 carbon‑steel segment. the replacement pipe was welded using a hot‑gas sleeve technique, tested under a 1200‑psi pressure test, and put back into service after a successful leak‑test. no injuries were reported, and the overpass construction schedule was only delayed by a few hours.

on april 12th 2025, an accidental ground displacement caused a 12‑inch carbon‑steel natural gas pipeline operating at 1,800 psi to rupture. the incident was discovered when a nearby construction crew using a 40‑ton hydraulic jack to stabilize a road grade inadvertently struck the pipe, resulting in a 2‑inch diameter fracture and a rapid release of gas. the operator immediately isolated the affected 5‑km segment, depressurizing the line from 1,800 to 600 psi over 45 minutes. no injuries were reported. the incident was reported to the local fire department at 09:12 am, to the state natural‑gas commission at 10:05 am, and to the national response center at 11:30 am. the pipeline was a 12‑inch, 1000‑psi‑rated, 316 stainless‑steel line with an 8‑mm wall thickness, buried 6 m below the surface. damage assessment indicated a 0.5‑meter displacement of surrounding soil, consistent with a minor seismic event (magnitude 4.2) recorded by the regional seismograph. the incident is under investigation pursuant to section 191.3, and the operator updated the incident log on april 15 2025.

during routine maintenance of the 30‑inch carbon steel line (max operating pressure 3200 psi) in the harris county corridor, a heavy truck on the adjacent highway lost steering control and collided with a retaining wall, causing a 12‑foot collapse onto the pipeline. the impact produced a 4‑inch diameter gouge in the pipe wall and a 2‑inch deep crater at the fracture location. the collision also severed the surrounding vegetation, which fell onto the pipe and added additional loading. after the incident the crew immediately shut off the line, isolated the affected segment with a 12‑inch pressure vessel, and conducted a pressure test to 2000 psi to confirm no further leakage. a coring operation revealed that the gouge had penetrated 0.75 inch of wall thickness, leaving a residual wall of 0.5 inch. the failure analysis attributed the rupture to the combined effect of the direct mechanical impact and the subsequent weight of the fallen trees. the repair plan involved removing the damaged 75‑foot section, installing a new 30‑inch seamless steel pipe, and performing a hydrostatic test at 3500 psi before re‑inserting the line into service.

on august 14, 2024, a maintenance crew on the 50‑year‑old 30‑inch, api 5l grade b, stainless steel line in the mid‑west encountered an unexpected rupture near a shallow water crossing. the incident was traced to a large commercial dredger that had been operating nearby to clear sediment for a new irrigation project. the dredger's suction head inadvertently created a high‑pressure jet that struck the exposed pipeline segment, exceeding the pipe’s maximum operating pressure of 3500 psi and causing a transverse fracture. the crew noted a sudden pressure drop from 2800 psi to 600 psi in the downstream pressure transmitter and heard a distinct “pop” audible over the control room. upon investigation, the fracture exhibited ductile tearing with a 30‑degree shear lip and a small ductile dimpling pattern on the inner surface, suggesting an overload event. the pipe material was api 5l grade b with a typical ferrite‑pearlite microstructure and a hardness of 95 hrb. the incident resulted in the release of approximately 1,200 mcf of natural gas, all of which was vented to a safe pressure line. a supplemental nrc report (report number 1187643) was filed on 2024‑08‑15, detailing the event and corrective actions, including a temporary relocation of the line and a new inspection regime for third‑party activities in the area.

at approximately 07:45 hrs on march 3, 2026, a heavy equipment crew operating a backhoe at the south side of interstate 70 right of way struck the external sleeve of a 12‑inch diameter, 3200‑psi polyethylene gas line located at the 3.8‑mile marker of the eastbound lane. the collision caused a rupture of the outer sheath and exposed the line to a sharp edge on the backhoe bucket, resulting in a 4‑inch circumferential gouge. gas control immediately lost pressure on index 321‑06 at 07:55 hrs and dispatched the pipeline crew. the crew arrived at the site at 08:20 hrs, isolated the segment by closing the adjacent 2.0‑inch isolation valve and verified a pressure drop to 45 psi. an evacuation of the surrounding residential zone up to 1/4 mile was ordered by local authorities. a field pressure test confirmed a 300‑psi loss and the decision was made to replace the 12‑inch pipe section. the replacement was completed at 12:45 hrs, and the line was restored to operating pressure of 3150 psi by 13:30 hrs. the pipeline was declared in service and traffic was cleared by 14:00 hrs.

on october 12, 2024, at approximately 9:45 a.m., a heavy construction crane operating on the south side of the river inadvertently contacted a buried 24-inch schedule 80 steel transmission line during excavation for a new highway. the impact caused a 4‑inch circumferential crack in the pipe wall. pressure sensors recorded a rapid pressure drop from 2,200 psi to 1,200 psi within 15 seconds. immediate isolation was executed by closing the upstream and downstream valves via the scada system. the incident was reported to the state environmental protection agency and the pipeline safety organization within 30 minutes. emergency crews from the local fire department arrived at 10:00 a.m. and confirmed that no gas was released to the atmosphere. the crack was inspected by the pipeline's corrosion monitoring team using ultrasonic thickness gauging, which confirmed a loss of 0.25 inches. a temporary repair clamp was installed by a licensed technician at 1:30 p.m., and the line was brought back to service at 4:00 p.m. after a pressure test at 1,800 psi confirmed integrity. no personnel injuries were reported and the surrounding area was cleared within two hours.

on may 15th, 2024, a local construction crew operating a skid steer on the north side of the 345‑210 line at the 345‑210‑south junction struck a section of the 8‑inch schedule‑80 steel pipe located 18 feet above grade. the impact caused the pipe to bend and the downstream 1‑inch high‑head valve to shear off the threaded connection to the elbow. operations received the call from the site manager at 08:32 am and dispatched a field crew within fifteen minutes. upon arrival the crew observed a 2‑inch diameter breach in the pipe and a 1‑inch valve stem that had separated from its housing. the crew immediately isolated the segment using the 345‑210‑south isolation valve and performed a blow‑down of the affected line. no gas was released during the blow‑down, and there were no injuries. a bypass was installed using a 6‑inch flexible hose and pressure‑rated fittings to maintain service to the downstream facilities. a full pressure test at 420 psig confirmed integrity of the bypass. the damaged pipe was replaced with a new 8‑inch schedule‑80 carbon steel pipe, welded shut, and the line was brought back online at 14:05 pm. the site was closed to traffic until the replacement was inspected and cleared by the regional inspection team.

dispatcher notified the on‑call engineer at 09:12 a.m. on march 18, 2024, reporting a collision between a construction crane and an 8‑inch (20 cm) steel line near the county landfill. the crane operator lost balance while repositioning a 12‑tonne boom, and the hook snagged the pipe, causing a 2‑inch segment to break and the line to rupture. the section was operating at 1,200 psig at the time of impact. the line was isolated by the upstream pressure control valve, and the downstream valve was closed under manual override. the engineer instructed the crew to conduct a rapid blowdown, which was completed by 10:45 a.m. with the line reduced to 30 psig. the damaged segment was identified by the pipe inspection tool; a 2‑inch weld‑to‑pipe section was completely severed and a 4‑inch section of the pipe wall had a 90‑degree crack. the crew removed the broken pipe, replaced it with a 2‑inch section, and welded a 6‑inch transition to the 8‑inch line. a hydrostatic test at 1,400 psig confirmed integrity. the line was purged, re‑pressurized, and service was restored at 04:30 p.m. the incident was reported to the state agency and an investigation was opened by the local construction authority. the estimated repair cost was $125,600.

on june 14, 2025, at approximately 03:07 am, a rupture was identified on a 24‑inch, 3500‑psi, x70 carbon steel pipeline operated by northern pipelines, l.l.c. the event occurred 145 feet downstream of the midtown compressor station, in an area adjacent to a municipal utility corridor. an underground construction crew operating a hydraulic excavator in the adjacent right‑of‑way inadvertently struck the pipeline, creating a 3‑inch gouge that progressed to a 4‑inch full‑length breach. the immediate pressure drop from 3500 to 1800 psi caused a sudden release of 12,000 barrels of crude oil, which spilled into a nearby drainage ditch and ignited due to an open spark from the excavator's electric equipment. by 03:25 am, the fire had spread along a 30‑foot segment of the pipe, prompting the on‑site gas‑control operator to initiate an emergency shut‑down of the entire line at 03:30 am. the fire suppression team, consisting of 5 fire engines and 3 aerial units, arrived at 03:45 am and began water deluge operations. the incident was reported to the state energy commission at 04:10 am and to the national response center at 04:30 am. the spill was contained, no injuries were reported, and the damaged pipe segment was replaced during the following week, with a 30‑day shutdown of the line.

on april 22, 2024, at approximately 04:15 am local time, a municipal maintenance crew was conducting routine grading near the 18‑inch schedule 80 carbon steel natural gas line that runs from the northfield distribution hub to the eastern rural service corridor. an accidental collision with a 200‑cubic‑foot high‑bed tractor caused the tractor’s front bumper to strike the pipeline’s support footing. the impact displaced the footing, causing a 12‑inch longitudinal crack in the pipe wall approximately 7 feet from the closest splice flange. pressure in the line at the time was 750 psi, and the rupture led to an uncontrolled gas release that rapidly increased the pressure in the adjacent segment to 1,100 psi before the automatic shut‑off valves engaged. the incident was reported to the local emergency management office and to the state natural gas regulator within 30 minutes. emergency responders closed the road, evacuated the surrounding residential zone, and secured the site. line integrity monitoring indicated a 5‑inch diameter loss of the pipe wall at the crack location. repair crews installed a temporary sleeve, isolated the segment, and conducted a pressure‑test of the affected section at 1,500 psi. full line replacement was completed by 08:45 on april 24, with pressure restored to 750 psi and service resumed to the hub. the incident was documented in nrc report 2024‑04567, with a final cost estimate of $127,890.

on march 15th at 9:42 am, a local construction crew was excavating for a new roadway near the 8‑inch schedule 80 steel gas line that runs from the refinery to the distribution hub. the pipe was operating at 2,600 psi at the time. a bulldozer operator misidentified the pipe as a buried utility and used a 14‑in blade to clear the site. the blade impact severed the pipe approximately 1.5 inches in diameter at the mid‑span of the trench, creating an immediate gas release. a resident called 911 at 9:45 am, reporting a strong odor and flames near the intersection. emergency services arrived by 9:50 am and heard the hissing. the pipeline operator shut down the line by pulling the main isolation valve at 9:52 am, reducing the pressure to 0 psi. a repair crew arrived at 10:15 am, secured the area with a temporary gas lock and placed a 12‑inch steel flange on both ends of the damaged section. the pipe was cut, the broken segment removed, and a new 8‑inch pipe was installed and welded in place by 12:30 pm. the line was brought back online at 1:00 pm after pressure testing at 800 psi with no leaks. the incident was reported to the nrc within 30 minutes and a formal incident report was filed with phmsa on march 18th.

on april 12, 2023, at approximately 07:45 am local time, a routine inspection of the 18‑inch schedule‑80 steel gas transmission line crossing the creeks of the mid‑south region revealed a 2‑inch longitudinal crack in the pipe near the 2,345‑ft elevation splice. the line, operated by mid‑south pipelines, was carrying natural gas at a design pressure of 1,200 psi. a construction company, mid‑south construction, had recently installed a 60‑foot high crane for bridge reinforcement adjacent to the pipeline corridor. the crane operator inadvertently dropped a 12‑ton load, which struck the pipeline at 07:32 am, causing a sudden depressurization to 350 psi and a catastrophic rupture. the rupture released an estimated 5,600 cfm of gas, forming a 60‑meter radius plume that ignited upon contact with a nearby electrical line at 07:38 am, resulting in a small fire. mid‑south pipelines crew isolated the line at 07:45 am and deployed a portable flare system. the incident was reported to the nrc and the phmsa by 08:15 am. a preliminary assessment by a third‑party engineering firm identified a 3‑inch gouge and a 2‑inch transverse fracture in the pipe wall. the repair plan includes a 18‑inch splice and re‑gassing the line to 1,200 psi, expected to be completed by 02:30 pm on april 15, 2023. updates will be submitted to the cpcu and cpuc as required.

on 12/07/2023 a coastal construction crew operating a 55‑tonne jackhammer within the 3,200‑ft radius of the gulf south trans‑gulf pipeline breached a section of 8‑inch carbon‑steel line at the 7,245‑ft depth. the jackhammer, positioned to loosen bedrock for a new marina berm, was inadvertently shifted 2 ft by a sudden wind gust, causing the vibration to transmit to the pipe. the impact created a 3‑inch circumferential crack and released 12,000 psi of pressure into the surrounding silt, spiking the surface flow to 2,500 ft³/h. a pressure relief valve located at the 7,240‑ft depth automatically opened, preventing a catastrophic rupture. after the crew secured the area, the crew supervisor dispatched a remotely operated vehicle (rov) to assess the damage. the rov footage revealed a partially fractured weld and a 1‑inch loss of wall thickness. the pipeline was shut down, the damaged segment was cut out, and a 1‑inch stainless‑steel replacement section was installed using an automated welding rig. the line was restored to service at 10,500 psi after a series of pressure tests and ultrasonic inspections. the incident was documented under third‑party construction impact, and a mitigation plan was submitted to the regulatory authority to prevent future jackhammer‑related breaches.

on august 2, 2024, a 22‑inch natural gas transmission line (material: alloy 80 stainless steel, operating pressure 1,200 psi) crossing the ridge of the northern foothills of the blue ridge was compromised during a sudden seismic event. the tremor, rated 5.8 on the richter scale, caused a 1.5‑meter displacement of the soil adjacent to the pipeline, producing a sharp bend in the line. within ten minutes of the quake, the bent section experienced a sudden pressure surge to 1,450 psi as the pipe wall thinned from 0.312 to 0.081 inches at the fracture point. a rupture occurred at the mid‑span, ejecting a 15‑foot fragment of pipe and releasing a plume of gas that ignited when it contacted a nearby abandoned logging fire. emergency response crews from the state fire marshal and the local gas company arrived within 12 minutes, isolated the section via the nearest isolation valve at 1,150 psi, and shut in the line. the incident resulted in a 600‑foot loss of line, a 25‑meter crater, and a temporary shutdown of 60 miles of downstream pipeline. a post‑incident investigation confirmed that the damage was caused by the seismic event and subsequent soil movement, with no evidence of corrosion or material failure.

on 5/17/2024 at 11:45 am eastern daylight time the regional operations center received a report from a local municipal maintenance crew about a sudden drop in pressure in the 8‑inch carbon steel transmission line that serves the south‑side industrial park. the crew had been performing a routine street‑cleaning operation when a large, over‑grown oak branch fell from the adjacent property and struck the pipe near mile marker 73.8. the impact caused a 2‑inch longitudinal crack on the pipe’s outer surface and a sudden release of the 1,200‑psi line pressure. the field crew arrived on site at 12:12 pm and immediately shut the downstream relief valve; a temporary bypass was installed on the 12‑inch sleeve pipe to maintain service to the downstream district. by 1:03 pm the pressure had normalized at 1,050 psi and the crack was isolated with a welded plug. the 8‑inch line was inspected with a 6‑inch ultrasonic probe, and the crack measured 1.5 inches in length. repairs were scheduled for 6/3/2024 with a full line replacement to be completed by 6/28/2024. the incident was reported to the state regulator on 5/19/2024.

on tuesday, march 12, 2025, at approximately 08:45 am, a construction crew operating a 200-ton hydraulic jack on the southbound shoulder of interstate 75 near mile marker 47 accidentally struck a buried 24-inch diameter steel gas pipeline owned by west valley gas. the pipeline, rated at 260 psig and constructed of carbon steel with a 0.06-inch wall thickness, suffered a transverse rupture at the impact site, resulting in an uncontrolled release of natural gas. the crew immediately stopped operations and called 911. emergency responders isolated the affected segment by closing the downstream valve at the west valley gas substation and shutting the upstream mainline at the northern junction. the gas leak was contained within a 30-foot radius and no injuries were reported. west valley gas technicians assessed the damage and performed a temporary repair by installing a 12-inch bypass line with a pressure rating of 280 psig. the temporary repair was completed at 14:30 on march 12. permanent repairs, including replacement of the damaged 24-inch pipe segment and re‑insertion of a 10% carbon steel flange, are scheduled for april 20, 2025. the incident was reported to the national response center at 17:00 on march 12.

at approximately 15:45 hrs on 06/12/2025, an automated delivery truck operated by a local logistics company was making a left turn at the intersection of county road 27 and river street in south bay county, texas. a sudden loss of traction on a wet curb caused the truck to veer off the roadway, striking a 30‑inch welded carbon‑steel transmission pipeline that ran adjacent to the street. the impact sheared a 10‑foot section of pipe, instantly releasing the 9500‑psi service pressure. the truck driver was taken to the emergency department with minor injuries. within five minutes the local fire department crews isolated the pipeline by shutting the remote control valve located 1200 ft downstream. gas company field crews arrived at 15:58 hrs, evaluated the damage, and began controlled venting of the exposed line to relieve pressure. by 16:15 hrs the pipeline was shut in and a temporary splice was installed. the line was inspected, pressure tested, and brought back to service at 18:40 hrs. the incident was reported to the state environmental agency within 24 hours. no environmental releases were documented.

on february 7, 2025 at 10:15 am central standard time, a municipal maintenance crew was excavating a sidewalk under a 26‑inch steel propane line operating at 300 psi in the 7500 block of oak street, denver, co. while using a hydraulic backhoe, the crew inadvertently struck the pipe with a dropped concrete block. the impact produced a 2‑inch rupture in the steel line. the crew immediately shut in the line with a remote‑controlled valve located 200 feet upstream. pressure fell to 0 psi within 45 seconds and a small leak was detected by the on‑site gas detector. the local fire department was notified and a two‑hour response was dispatched. a 120‑foot section of the pipe was cut out and replaced with a 26‑inch seamless steel splice. the replacement pipe was a 4‑inch schedule 80 steel section rated for 350 psi and was installed using a hot‑fitting technique. the line was pressure‑tested to 350 psi and pressure was restored to 300 psi. an update was filed with the colorado public utilities commission at 2:00 pm cst, and the incident was closed with no loss of service to the community.

on june 12, 2024, at 09:17 am local time, midwest interstate gas transmission (midwest igt) dispatch received a notification from a municipal contractor about a potential collision at the south side of the river crossing on e‑472. the incident involved a 45‑tonne tower crane that had been operating on the right‑hand side of the highway overpass to remove a damaged guardrail. due to a sudden wind gust, the crane’s jib descended and contacted a 36‑inch, 420‑psi, carbon‑steel pipeline carrying natural gas from the prairie field to the eastern distribution hub. the impact severed a 12‑inch flange section and caused a localized pressure drop to 200 psi. crew members immediately shut down the upstream valve, isolated the affected segment, and performed a pressure test that confirmed containment. the damaged flange was removed, a splice collar was installed, and the line was re‑pressurized to 415 psi after a successful leak check. no personnel injuries were reported and no gas was released to the atmosphere. the incident was logged in the national response center as report no. 20240612. engineering evaluation concluded that the collision was due to an external mechanical force, and the pipeline was deemed operable after repairs.

on march 15, 2024, a municipal maintenance crew was using a hydraulic excavator to remove debris from the south side of riverview road when the arm struck an underground 10‑inch crimped steel pipe carrying 800 psi natural gas. the impact displaced the pipe, creating a 1‑inch breach in the outer surface. gas began leaking onto the road surface at approximately 0630. the crew immediately shut off the adjacent isolating valve at 0635, and local fire department was notified at 0638. emergency responders arrived at 0645 and secured the area, evacuating a 200‑meter radius due to the risk of ignition. the pipeline company dispatched a pressure reduction team, lowering the system pressure from 800 to 500 psi by 0700. a field inspection revealed a fractured weld and a cracked 3‑inch section of the pipe. repairs commenced at 1500 the same day, involving replacement of a 4‑foot segment and re‑crimping of the fittings. the line was restored to service at 2100 after leak testing. no injuries or customer outages were reported. the incident was recorded as an outside force damage event.

on july 14, 2024 at 08:42 am a heavy construction crane operator inadvertently dropped a steel anchor onto a 20‑inch stainless steel gas line located at the 2,500‑foot marker of the eastward branch of the larkspur gas transmission system. the impact fractured the pipe near the joint and created a 2‑inch breach, resulting in a rapid pressure drop from 1250 psi to 650 psi within 45 seconds. emergency system control was notified by the crew at 08:55 am, and the automated shut‑off valves were engaged at 09:02 am, isolating the affected segment. the incident team arrived on site at 09:15 am, confirmed the rupture and performed a visual inspection of the surrounding trench. a leak survey using a gas detector array indicated a vapor plume extending approximately 60 meters. the line was re‑pressurized to 800 psi at 10:30 am after a temporary repair was completed with a 6‑foot section of 20‑inch seamless pipe and a flared gasket seal. a full line integrity test was conducted at 12:45 pm, showing a pressure tolerance of 1450 psi and no further leaks. the incident was closed at 02:00 pm with a report filed to the state regulator. no injuries or customer impact were recorded.

on monday, april 12, 2024, a 10‑inch wrought‑iron natural gas pipeline operating at 250 psi intersected a newly laid highway in the rural county of jones. during excavation the construction crew accidentally drove an 18‑ton jackhammer over the pipe, fracturing the pipe near a welded sleeve and creating a 12‑inch rupture. a sudden release of gas generated a visible vapor plume that drifted downwind toward the nearby residential area. local fire department units arrived within 2 minutes; the crew shut down the main line by actuating the upstream 20‑inch isolation valve located 150 feet downstream of the fault. the emergency response plan was activated, establishing a safe perimeter and deploying portable gas detectors. a 12‑inch temporary repair flange was installed, and a welded patch was applied to close the rupture. after confirming a leak‑free condition with a 75‑psi pressure test, the line was brought back to service at 210 psi on april 15, 2024. the incident was reported to the state regulator as a non‑violent release, and no injuries were documented.

on april 3, 2024 at 10:12 a.m., a local county fire department responded to a reported gas odor at the intersection of 5th street and river road in springfield. the incident involved a 12‑inch carbon steel transmission main carrying natural gas at an operating pressure of 275 psig, located beneath a newly constructed residential driveway. initial field tests detected a gas concentration of 22 % near the curb, prompting the immediate shutdown of the nearest 3‑way valve and the deployment of the county’s gas emergency response crew. upon arrival, the crew discovered that the main had a circumferential rupture approximately 3 inches in diameter, with evidence of a high‑energy impact. preliminary assessments suggested that the failure was caused by an over‑tensioned construction cable that had inadvertently pulled through the pipe during a recent excavation for a storm drain. the gas distribution company dispatched a pressure test crew to isolate the damaged segment, which was sealed by installing a temporary steel cap. a full leak survey was conducted, and a pressure‑hold test confirmed no further leaks. the main was repaired with a 12‑inch carbon‑steel sleeve and welded shut, and service was restored at 15:48 after a 90‑minute outage. the incident was documented and reported to the psc, phmsa, and local regulatory agencies.

at approximately 3:12 p.m. on july 15, 2025, the county public works crew was excavating a new stormwater drain along the northern side of the raleigh‑swan river, located near the junction of state route 78 and county road 12. the crew was using a hydraulic excavator with a 2‑foot bucket when the machine’s hydraulic line broke and the bucket tipped onto a nearby 10‑inch cross‑connected polyethylene gas line that had been buried 18 in. below the riverbank at the 2.3 mile mark. the gas line was operating at 142 psig and had a nominal wall thickness of 0.25 in. the impact severed the pipe, creating a 6‑inch longitudinal fracture and releasing a rapid burst of methane into the air. a local resident in the adjacent culvert heard a sharp pop and reported the incident to the regional emergency dispatch at 3:17 p.m. the dispatch notified the state natural resources agency and the regional pipeline operator, sierra‑gas. sierra‑gas dispatchers dispatched a mobile line‑repair crew to the site, and by 3:55 p.m. a temporary plug had been installed and the line was isolated. the county fire department secured the area and the state wildlife agency conducted a rapid water sampling test that confirmed no surface contamination. an on‑site investigation was conducted by sierra‑gas engineering and the county civil engineer. the investigation concluded that the hydraulic failure of the excavator and the lack of a pre‑excavation survey constituted the immediate cause of the rupture. the incident was reported to the environmental protection agency, and a corrective action plan was submitted to the state pipeline safety office, which includes mandatory pre‑excavation training for all county crews and the installation of a 24‑hour monitoring system on the 10‑inch line segment.

on march 3, 2024, a 16 in. schedule 80 steel transmission line carrying natural gas at 750 psi experienced a rupture near the junction of corridor 12, 45 miles west of city x. the failure was traced to a 6 ft. trenching operation by a local contractor that had inadvertently removed a portion of the concrete support wall, exposing the pipe to the 4.5 ton excavator wheel. an inspection crew noted a 1 in. circumferential crack in the pipe wall, approximately 10 ft. from the ground surface, coinciding with the trench edge. field crew replaced the damaged segment with a 16 in. x 30 ft. seamless steel pipe, pressure tested to 1200 psi with a 5‑min hold, and reconnected the line. a temporary shut‑off valve was installed 50 ft. upstream for monitoring. the incident report was filed with phmsa on march 6, 2024. additional data required by phmsa regarding the trench dimensions and wheel load was supplied on march 10. no gas loss or casualties were reported. the pipeline operator issued a safety notice to all contractors in the area regarding proper trenching near existing lines.

on october 17, 2026 at approximately 07:42 a.m., a fallen utility pole from a severe windstorm struck a buried 10‑inch natural gas pipeline at mile marker 12.3 near cedar ridge. the impact produced a 2‑inch breach, releasing gas at about 850 psi. crew crews located the leak within 12 minutes, shut the upstream isolation valve, and vented the pressure to a designated vent line. no ignition occurred and the surrounding area remained unburned. the crew installed a temporary repair clamp and pressure‑tested the repaired section at 700 psi. the segment was returned to service on october 20, 2026 at 02:00 p.m. there were no injuries or property damage reported. the incident was confirmed by company personnel at 09:00 a.m., and a notification was filed with phmsa on october 20, 2026. a preliminary investigation determined the damage resulted from wind‑generated debris impacting the pipeline, classifying the event as outside force damage. for additional information, contact j. smith at 555‑123‑4567.

on 6/15/2023, a severe nor'easter produced a 4‑foot high surge that washed a 28‑inch schedule 80 carbon steel transmission line from the protective berm into the open sea off the coast of south carolina. the pipe, operating at 1,200 psi, was exposed at junction 4. an eyewitness noted a large boulder, estimated at 15,000 lb, was propelled by the surge and struck the pipe at a 90‑degree angle, creating a 3‑foot long gouge and a 12‑inch diameter perforation. pressure readings at the upstream valve dropped from 1,190 psi to 560 psi within 18 minutes, indicating a significant leak. the crew deployed a temporary shoring system and installed a 6‑foot long pressure‑rated splice to isolate the damaged section. a full‑scale hydrostatic test at 1,250 psi was conducted to confirm integrity of the remaining line. the incident was logged as an outside‑force damage event, and the investigation determined the failure was attributable to the storm‑generated debris impact, with no evidence of intentional or accidental human interference.

on may 12, 2024, a routine excavation by a local contractor near the confluence of river x in county y inadvertently struck the 48‑inch stainless steel line 3‑21 of the east river transmission system. the pipe, operating at 1600 psi and 3500 scfd, experienced a sudden drop in pressure to 200 psi within 3 minutes. a burst was observed at the 1120 ft marker, releasing approximately 45,000 cubic feet of natural gas. the contractor had not activated the one‑call system before work commenced, and the pipeline location marker was not visible due to recent vegetation growth. temporary repairs involved installing a 6‑inch steel sleeve coupler and a stop valve at the 1110 ft marker, followed by a line isolation at the 1060 ft remote valve. the incident was reported to the state regulator at 11:25 a.m., and local fire and emergency medical services were dispatched to the scene. a field inspection by the operator’s crew confirmed a transverse shear fracture at the outer diameter, consistent with an impact from a hydraulic jackhammer. repairs were completed on may 15, 2024, with a full 48‑inch line replacement scheduled for completion in early june. all relevant agencies received the incident report per regulatory requirements.

in the afternoon of august 15, 2024, a construction crew operating a jackhammer near the intersection of highway 12 and river road inadvertently struck a buried 24‑inch diameter carbon steel line that was carrying 1200 psi natural gas to the regional distribution center. the crew had been excavating for a new sewer line and had not been notified of the pipeline location due to a lapse in the utility coordination database. the impact ruptured a 3‑foot section of the line, causing a rapid release of gas into the surrounding soil. the gas plume spread along the highway shoulder, and a nearby parked vehicle ignited when a spark from the jackhammer struck the vapor cloud. no fatalities occurred, but three occupants of the vehicle received second‑degree burns and were treated at the county medical center. the pipeline operator shut down the line via a remote command at 14:32, isolating the 30‑mile section downstream. the damaged segment was replaced with a new 24‑inch carbon steel pipe, welded using tig welding under a pressure test of 1500 psi, and the line was re‑commissioned at 18:15. the incident was reported to the state phmsa and a preliminary investigation found that the lack of updated pipeline registry data was the root cause. total repair costs were estimated at $125,000, including labor, materials, and environmental remediation.

on 6/14/2024 at 0930 hours a local forestry crew reported that a storm‑tipped maple had fallen onto the 24‑inch diameter, 300‑psi, 80‑year‑old steel pipeline near milepost 15.6 in the northern county. field ops dispatched a gas‑line crew at 1005 hours. upon arrival at 1045 hours, the crew observed a 5‑inch longitudinal crack in the pipe with gas pressure at 310 psi. the crack was located on the downstream side of the 24‑inch pipe, which is part of the main transmission line supplying the regional power plant. the crew performed an emergency pressure relief by opening the emergency shut‑off valve at the 24‑inch control station, reducing pressure to 120 psi, and isolated the section. the fire‑resistant valve was then closed to prevent gas escape. a 12‑inch, 250‑psi, stainless steel repair sleeve was installed, and the line was brought back to service after a pressure test at 280 psi. the incident was logged in the daily operation report and the affected segment was marked for replacement within the next quarter. the crew noted that the maple was in a 15‑foot canopy, and the root system had penetrated the trench, causing the pipe to shift and fracture. the incident was reported to the state environmental agency for compliance.

on april 23, 2024 at 2:15 p.m., a construction crane operating on county road 72 collapsed onto a 48‑inch carbon steel transmission line (pipe number 4021) located at 45.123456 -94.654321. the impact severed a 6‑foot section and caused the line to rupture, releasing approximately 4.3 million cubic feet of natural gas. the crane operator lost control while moving the boom, the crane fell, and struck the pipeline. the crane was 3,200 pounds, the operator was 65 years old, and the crane was 25 feet high. upon the event, the crew at the site closed the nearest 2‑inch isolation valve and notified the local emergency response. the blowdown was completed at 4:00 p.m., and the line was brought down to 0 psi by 5:30 p.m. at 8:45 p.m. a field crew isolated the leak and sealed the damaged section with a 6‑inch flange repair kit. a 12‑mile segment was pulled down for replacement. the repair was finished on april 28, 2024 after pressure testing at 1,800 psi. the incident was reported to the nrc and the state public utility commission.

on april 14, 2024, neptune energy's 48‑inch class 3 natural gas line at the junction of route 12 and highway 101 was found damaged following a heavy truck collision with the pipeline support structure during a municipal road repair. the incident was reported by the county engineer at 09:23 a.m. local time. the pipe, made of carbon steel with an a106 grade b wall thickness of 0.5 inches, had been under 180 psi operating pressure. the truck, weighing 40,000 lbs, struck the steel girder that was anchoring the pipe to the ground, causing a 5‑inch longitudinal fracture near the mid‑span. initial field inspection confirmed the leak and the line was isolated by closing the upstream valve at 09:55 a.m. dcp gas control technicians arrived at 10:20 a.m. and performed a pressure test. the failure was documented as a fatigue crack induced by the impact loading. a metallurgical lab analysis later showed a brittle‑ductile transition fracture with a high‑stress concentration at the weld foot. the line was purged and capped; a temporary diversion was installed. a supplemental 30‑day report was filed on april 20, 2024, noting that the site had been cleared and no further service will resume until the county completes the road rehabilitation and provides new construction drawings.

on 06-14-2024 at 03:27 a sudden heavy windstorm caused a mature oak to fall onto the 20-inch high pressure steel pipeline located at mile marker 42.5 in the vicinity of the green river valley. the impact ruptured the pipe at the 42.7 mark, resulting in an immediate pressure drop from 350 psi to 210 psi as the gas escaped through the break. within 7 minutes the control center isolated the section between the 42.4 and 43.0 valve, and the line was blown down at 04:05. the rupture produced a cloud of gas that ignited a brief flare observed at 04:12. no injuries were reported. emergency crews arrived by 04:30 and began containment procedures. on 06-15-2024 a field crew assessed the damage and estimated the break to be 3 feet in length. a replacement section of 20-inch carbon steel pipe, 3.2-inch schedule 80, was installed on 06-18-2024 with pressure testing at 350 psi for 15 minutes. the line was brought back online at 06-19-2024 at 09:00, and normal operations resumed by 10:15.

at 14:23 on 9/18/2022, a local construction crew was excavating a storm drain near the intersection of 4th and main in the south‑bound corridor. the crew employed a hydraulic jackhammer on a 1.5‑meter concrete slab that had been removed for new paving. while working, the jackhammer struck a 4‑inch diameter seamless carbon‑steel line that had been buried 1.2 meters underground and was operating at 350 psi of natural gas. the impact produced a 1‑inch circumferential nick on the pipe’s outer surface, immediately compromising the wall thickness. gas control received a report of pressure drop at 14:35, and dispatch closed the nearest isolation valve at 14:38. the line’s downstream pressure fell from 345 psi to 210 psi within 4 minutes, and a 30‑cubic‑meter burst of gas was released into the surrounding soil. responders from the gas control team arrived by 14:55 and identified the nicked section about 350 feet from the nearest highway. a field‑rigged split‑sleeve repair was performed at 15:20, sealing the breach and restoring pressure to 335 psi after 15 minutes of work. the incident was reported to the regulatory authority at 16:45 after the repair cost was calculated to exceed the reporting threshold.

on april 17, 2025 at 13:12 local time, east valley natural gas pipeline company (evng) reported a rupture on the 6‑inch, 1400‑psi interstate line near the ridge of greenfield county. the damage was caused by a heavy construction crane operating on a nearby road that inadvertently contacted the buried pipe; the crane operator was unaware of the pipeline location, and the hydraulic arm struck the pipe, creating a 12‑inch breach. the gas transmission line was isolated by the automatic pressure relief valve at 13:35, and the emergency shutdown system closed the upstream compressor station. field crews removed the damaged section and installed a new 6‑inch forged steel replacement segment at 18:45 after a pressure test at 1450 psi. the line was brought back to service at 20:30, with no injuries or fire reported. the incident was reported to the state department of energy and the pipeline authority because the estimated repair cost exceeded $85,000, and local authorities closed road 22 during the response.
